text:
alex: FYI customer POC hitting two things: fn_call responses sometimes have required fields as null when we run in JSON mode, and their infra is intermittently reporting SSL handshake errors. need quick triage, this is blocking demo tomorrow.

morgan: can you paste a raw example of the fn_call output that has nulls? is it always the same field(s)?

alex: here's one (redacted):
```
{"tool":"invoice_parser","name":"parse_invoice","arguments":{"invoice_id":null,"total":null,"vendor":"Acme"}}
```
fields invoice_id and total become null about 15% of calls. when we toggle off structured/JSON mode, the same prompt yields a plain text parse we can regex against.

jia: do we have request_id or trace id for those failing calls? also which model + max_tokens?

alex: request_id: r-8f7a2c9e; model: r-infer-1-large; max_output_tokens: 512; prompt length ~420 tokens; streaming enabled.

eli: first suspicion: truncation + JSON parser strictness. if the model's completion is cut mid-object, our JSON strict mode will fail and we may map missing keys to null. any logs showing truncated content or "incomplete output"?

alex: not in app logs, customer reported they see the envelope with nulls intermittently. i attached the raw completion to the ticket, looks like trailing garbage in some cases: `}\nextra text`

morgan: also check for UTF-8 BOM or weird charset. we had a previous POC where the content started with a BOM and our parser mis-read the first char, shifting offsets and breaking the schema match. is the customer on Windows-based extractor?

caroline: on the security side they asked about TLS settings for Private deployment earlier — the SSL handshake errors might be their proxy (they have a corporate TLS inspection appliance). infra-bot logs: TLS_ERROR on upstream: `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate` for some connections.

infra-bot: [deploy-connector] 1749004360 TRACE r-8f7a2c9e upstream_tls: handshake failed, subject CN mismatch, peer_cert_chain len=0, retry scheduled.

jia: that error points to their proxy not presenting a full chain. ask them to verify proxy presents CA chain or add our root CA to their trust store. meanwhile, for the fn_call nulls, two quick mitigation options: 1) switch off strict JSON mode (use relaxed/regex fallback) 2) increase max_output_tokens and add an explicit end-of-json sentinel in the prompt like `\n---END_JSON---` and trim after that.

eli: also try: wrap the function output in a labeled codeblock in the prompt and require the model to respond only with the codeblock. e.g. `Respond with only a JSON object inside ```json ... ``` and nothing else.` that reduces model extra text.

alex: can we push a temporary server-side parser fallback that attempts to recover partial JSON? customer can't change proxy config before demo.

morgan: yes we can add a tolerant post-processor that tries to extract the first top-level JSON object using a bracket-balancing scan, then run a best-effort JSON fix (remove trailing text, fix unclosed arrays). that is engineering work but doable as a POC patch. estimate ~2 dev-days.

caroline: for the SSL issue, offer two options to customer: 1) whitelist our outbound IPs and ensure TLS passthrough so their appliance doesn't terminate, or 2) install our CA in their inspection device. both are common for enterprise demos. note: they'll need security approval — mention in the QSA.

alex: pricing/sales ask: if we recommend increasing max_output_tokens or enabling retries we may increase cost — how to frame this to the customer?

salesbot: suggest framing as: "temporary mitigation to stabilize parsing for demo; engineering will ship a robust fix post-POC. any additional token cost is expected to be negligible for demo traffic and we'll share token usage estimates." :thumbsup:

jia: additional debugging asks: can you collect a failing request raw_response (base64 ok), the exact prompt + system message, and whether the client sent a Content-Type with charset (should be `application/json; charset=utf-8`). also capture the full TLS error from their proxy.

alex: will collect and upload to the ticket. quick workaround for demo: 1) disable strict JSON output in the POC integration 2) add sentinel `---END_JSON---` 3) enable tolerant post-processor on our side. we'll also ask customer to try a passthrough for TLS.

eli: one more tip: if you see `null` for numeric fields specifically, sometimes the model emits `NaN` or `—` which our strict coercer turns to null. add a normalization step that maps common placeholders to strings/numbers then validate.

morgan: i'll schedule the 2-day patch work and add a note on the ticket about rollback after demo. thanks.

alex: thanks everyone — i'll update customer and attach the debug artifacts.

caroline: i updated the QSA item: "network config options and suggested TLS passthrough" and asked for estimated timeline from customer security.

salesbot: customer reply pending. emoji :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: last message — ping me if customer can reproduce with a full raw_response; we'll prioritize.
